title: DC Leadership Changes Renew Interest in Constantine 2
excerpt:
A reported DC leadership transition has revived sequel discussions.
No official production greenlight or release date is established.
body_md:
Following reports that James Gunn and Peter Safran are leaving DC Studios, questions about the studio's film slate have intensified. One long-discussed project attracting renewed attention is a sequel to Constantine starring Keanu Reeves.

The report identifies Jeremy Latcham, who worked with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy, as the incoming studio chief. It remains unclear which elements of the previous DCU plan will survive. The article raises the possibility that a management change could benefit projects that have spent years in development.

Original Constantine director Francis Lawrence is described as optimistic about the sequel's prospects under the changed circumstances. However, the retrieved article text does not include his full direct comments or an official studio decision on production.

The 2005 film developed a devoted following despite Reeves' interpretation differing considerably from the comic-book character. Matt Ryan later portrayed John Constantine in NBC's short-lived 2014 series, before returning in the Arrowverse and animated productions.

Fan enthusiasm and potential changes in studio priorities do not amount to a production commitment. The available report establishes neither a filming schedule nor a release date for the sequel.
